transcript:
Header: 2026-12-08 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Record: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (AstraNexus Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (AstraNexus SRE), Sara Gomez (AstraNexus Director of Platform)

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is the QBR for AstraNexus, quick agenda — usage & cost, reliability, roadmap sync and next steps. how's everyone doing?
00:08 Priya Patel: good, thanks Maya. excited to dig in. we've had some spikes over the last month that pushed our cost up so want to understand options.
00:15 Liam O'Connor: yeah and we had a couple of latency blips around the 3pm PST window, probably correlated with batch jobs.
00:23 Daniel Park: ok good context. quick note, i'll call out some thread-level metrics and possible mitigations — batching config, prefix caching, and dedicated pool sizing.
00:35 Maya Chen: just to set expectations, we'll review the token usage graph, call out where tail latency increases, talk through hosting vs dedicated, and then action items.
01:02 Priya Patel: quick question — do you have any immediate suggestions on reducing cost without sacrificing latency? we've tried increasing batch size but it increased tail.
01:12 Daniel Park: yeah so that's the classic tradeoff; larger batches reduce cost but can increase p99. for your workload pattern — lots of short chat sessions interleaved with a small percentage of long generation — we recommended a mixed profile: small latency-first routes for interactive traffic, and a batch-optimized route for async generations. also KV cash — uh "KV cache" is super helpful for repeated prefixes, that can cut token compute.
01:34 Sara Gomez: spelling — KV cash, ha — but seriously, how invasive is that to add? our infra team is cautious about changing runtime config in prod.
01:43 Daniel Park: low invasiveness; it's a serving runtime toggle and we can stage it in canary. it does require model variant compat and a bit of warm-up. we can coordinate with your SREs.
01:58 Liam O'Connor: network and security are also big — we need VPC peering options and KMS integration for keys. our compliance team won't sign off until SOC2 materials are in place.
02:10 Maya Chen: understood — we have a Redwood security pack, SOC2 + ISO docs, and KMS integration guides. i'll attach the network diagrams and SAML/SSO options after.
02:21 Priya Patel: cool, please. also curious on the dedicated capacity pricing model; is there a spreadsheet we can run numbers through?
02:29 Maya Chen: yes, i'll send the updated pricing sheet. quick high-level: dedicated gives you predictable throughput and reserved GPUs which usually lowers unit cost for steady high-volume workloads; hosted is good for variable or lower volume.
02:43 Priya Patel: our volume is growing — roughly 2.2M tokens/day currently, but top 5% of days spike up to 6-7M.
02:53 Daniel Park: that's useful. if spikes are frequent, dedicated with burst policies or hybrid routing is often best: keep latency-critical traffic on a low-latency hosted route and route heavy async batches to dedicated or a cheaper quantized model.
03:10 Sara Gomez: how about the quantized model support? we tried a 4-bit variant with another vendor and saw regressions in answer quality.
03:20 Daniel Park: yep quality regressions are a risk. Redwood Optimize recommends model/quantization profiles per workload — we can run automatic evals against your prompt set to compare quality delta. that was one item on the roadmap we wanted to align on.
03:36 Priya Patel: perfect — can you run that eval on our 150 prompt testset?
03:41 Daniel Park: yes, we'll need a copy or sample; we can do a blind A/B and return delta metrics.
03:47 Maya Chen: i'll add that as an action item.
03:52 Liam O'Connor: operationally, SLOs — we need a 99.9% availability SLA and p95 latency under 400ms for interactive calls. are those realistic on hosted?
04:05 Daniel Park: hosted can hit p95 under 200-300ms in most regions, but availability SLAs are higher on Dedicated with contractual SLA. if you need 99.9% uptime and guaranteed capacity during spikes, Dedicated + burst or private deployment is the path.
04:24 Priya Patel: what's the timeline for private deployment? we might be required to go VPC or on-prem in H1.
04:31 Maya Chen: Private deployments take longer — typically a few months for VPC + KMS config and more for on-prem. we'll bring in our Private specialist if you're leaning that way.
04:40 Sara Gomez: and pricing for Private? is it a platform fee plus infra?
04:44 Maya Chen: yes, platform fee plus support and infra costs; usually we structure as an enterprise contract. i'll include a ballpark in the pricing doc.
04:52 Priya Patel: ok great. any competitor notes we should be aware of? we've been evaluating Anthropic for a while because of their latency claims, and also internal infra with NVIDIA Triton for on-prem.
05:03 Daniel Park: we often see teams trade off Titan-like acceleration with more ops burden; Redwood tries to balance runtime optimizations with ease of ops. we can share benchmark comparisons but we'll run a tailored benchmark for you.
05:16 Maya Chen: quick recap and next steps — i'll send pricing + security docs by tomorrow, Daniel will schedule sizing workshop and benchmark window, Priya will send token usage and the 150-prompt eval set, and we'll reconvene after the benchmark.
05:34 Priya Patel: sounds good. one last quick ask — can we get a breakdown of token unit cost by model variant and by hosted vs dedicated?
05:42 Maya Chen: yes, the pricing sheet will include per-token estimates and a sample cost model for your current usage.
05:48 Liam O'Connor: cool; i'll loop in infra on scheduling for the benchmark.
05:52 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the materials and calendar invites.
06:00 End of recording

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache), speaker overlaps noted, some proper nouns may be slightly off.

Attachments referenced: Redwood pricing-sheet-v3.xlsx (link), Redwood-Security-Pack.zip (link), dedicated-sizing-workbook.xlsx (link), eval-template.csv (link)
